title: When Will The Trump PAC Money Be Spent?
text:
When Will The Trump PAC Money Be Spent?

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 16 Sep 2026

Spare a thought for Scott Bessent. For weeks, the US Treasury secretary has put his credibility on the line and attempted to put a ceiling on the yields of long-dated US government bonds… only for President Donald Trump to unveil at his latest rally a new plan to send checks of US$5,000 to every American adult. A promise that would tack on an additional US$1.3trn to the existing US$40trn US government debt load. Of course, it is easy to be cynical about such an announcement. American voters are still waiting for the “tariff checks” they were supposed to receive on the back of the “liberation day tariffs” (as it turned out, the tariff money ended up in the pockets of Walmart, Costco, Target, Amazon… shareholders!). Still, the US$5,000 “special dividend” was meaningful in many different ways.The first is that Trump’s promise of a US$5,000 individual payout, contingent on the GOP carrying the House of Representatives and the Senate in the upcoming midterm elections, makes US policymaking look deeply unserious to the rest of the world. After all, the US is already running budget deficits of around 7% of GDP and twin deficits in the double digits. At this stage of the cycle, fiscal policy should be looking to tighten its belt instead of expanding the waistline. So for President Trump to advocate such pro-cyclical fiscal policy, combined with a US foreign policy that seems to no longer really distinguish between friends and foes, makes it increasingly likely that foreign investors will no longer be piling into US assets?
